clue.text: Succeed in getting apple, one over ten feet

blocks.note: to land something is to succeed in getting it, like a fish or a job
a crab is a small sour apple, the crab apple

explanation.surface: Someone manages to reach an apple by climbing more than ten feet up the tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ten feet' reads as a height, but it is a count of legs: crabs are decapods, so one stands over ten feet.
explanation.definitionFit: This crustacean walks on ten legs like every crab, so it is a creature standing over ten feet.

clue.text: An honoured companion with Russell, an old Greek

blocks.note: the indefinite article in its shorter form
Companion of Honour, a British order
George William Russell, the Irish poet, wrote under the pen name AE
taken as written

explanation.surface: A distinguished friend accompanies a man called Russell and an ancient Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: Russell looks like Bertrand Russell; it is the Irish poet who signed himself AE.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer calls the Greeks besieging Troy by this tribal name, so it denotes an ancient Hellene.

clue.text: Norfolk town to register as nonconformist

blocks.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, an English county
to enter a name is to register it

explanation.surface: Someone moves to a Norfolk town to sign up with a breakaway chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: In English church history, Protestants outside the established Church were called Nonconformists or by this synonym.

clue.text: Smuggled Benedictine — J that's irregular

blocks.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, as in gun-running
Dom is the title of a Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: A smuggled bottle of the monks' liqueur is somehow out of order.
explanation.walkthrough: The '— J' in the newspaper text gives no letters and looks like a print or scan flaw. Benedictine is also a liqueur, which makes 'smuggled' natural.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard, following no pattern or rule, is irregular in the sense of lacking order.

clue.text: By a third revision, the best cards get awards

indicators.note: a revision is a rewritten version, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
in bridge and whist the top cards (ace, king, queen, jack, ten) are honours

explanation.surface: After a third reshuffle of the hands, the top cards win the prizes.
explanation.walkthrough: These are the honours the British monarch gives out each year on the official birthday.
explanation.definitionFit: This annual list of knighthoods, OBEs and other decorations is a set of awards from the Crown.

clue.text: Divide pack again about wood

blocks.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about, concerning
deal is sawn pine or fir timber

explanation.surface: A card player splits the deck afresh, perhaps on a wooden table.
explanation.walkthrough: To deal cards is to divide the pack among the players.
explanation.definitionFit: Dealing hands distributes a deck of cards among players, so doing it once more is this word.

clue.text: Engineer Mp's recall

blocks.note: Royal Engineers, the army corps, abbreviated RE
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An engineer calls for the recall of his member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall' looks like an MP being sacked by voters; it is a plain verb, to bring to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something back to mind from memory is to recall it.

clue.text: After ten maybe drink makes one weave about

indicators.note: maybe signals one possible form of the word, so its letters can be arranged otherwise
after places the drink behind the rearranged number in the final word

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written
a common drink

explanation.surface: After ten o'clock, drinking makes a person stagger about.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a drunk weaving home late; 'weave about' is the definition, to wind around.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist strands around one another is to interlace them, weaving them together.

clue.text: What park keepers do at night on the canal?

definitions.text: What park keepers do at night

blocks.clueFragment: What park keepers do at night
blocks.note: first meaning: secure the entrances at closing time
second meaning: the hinged barriers that hold water in a canal chamber

explanation.walkthrough: Read first as a verb phrase, a keeper's evening task, then as a noun phrase for structures on a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: Keepers secure park entrances at dusk, and canals have hinged watertight barriers at each end of each chamber.

clue.text: Selected for Korea by Japanese

blocks.note: first meaning: picked out
second meaning: the name Japan used for Korea during its rule of the peninsula

explanation.surface: Someone is picked for a Korean posting by a Japanese employer.
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle means picked out, and the same spelling was Japan's official colonial name for Korea from 1910 to 1945.

clue.text: Right order to grotesque dreamer

blocks.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right
the Order of Merit, a British honour, abbreviated OM
antic as an adjective means grotesque or bizarre

explanation.surface: Someone sets a bizarre dreamer straight by giving the proper command.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealist with head in the clouds is often called this, a visionary who is impractical.

clue.text: If he's one of Titania's train, he's a monster

blocks.note: old subjunctive: 'be he' means 'if he is'
Moth is one of the fairies attending Titania in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: If a man is one of the fairy queen's attendants, he must be a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says its own wordplay: 'be he Moth' is archaic for 'if he is Moth', and read as one word it is the beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical beast in Job has become a general word for any huge, monstrous creature or thing.

clue.text: Forcing Smith to leave besieged town

indicators.note: something told to leave departs, so its letters go out of the word around it

blocks.note: the South African town held under siege for 217 days in the Boer War
a smith works iron, chemical symbol Fe

explanation.surface: A man named Smith is made to quit a town under siege.
explanation.walkthrough: Smith looks like a surname; it stands for the smith's metal, iron, whose symbol is taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: Compelling someone, as in 'making him go', is the same sense as forcing them.

clue.text: The strength of Kipling's first mine-sweeper

blocks.note: first meaning: from the saying that union, or togetherness, is strength
second meaning: the first boat named in the refrain of Kipling's poem Mine Sweepers

explanation.surface: A question about how powerful Kipling's earliest minesweeping vessel was.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's refrain runs 'Sent up Unity, Claribel, Assyrian, Stormcock, and Golden Gain', so the first sweeper is named in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially, togetherness gives a group its power, and Kipling gave that name to the first trawler sent out sweeping.

clue.text: Desperate for simply glorious land of song

blocks.note: surface reading: someone longing for a glorious country

blocks.clueFragment: for simply glorious land of song
blocks.note: setter's reading: the song is Land of Hope and Glory, and a land that is only glorious has lost the other noun

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for a splendid, music-filled homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: Land of Hope and Glory is the patriotic Elgar song; keep only the glory and the land is without hope. 'Land of song' tempts towards Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone desperate has lost all expectation of improvement, which is to be without any optimism.

clue.text: Cheese arrived with decoration, right?

blocks.note: past tense of come
Member of the Order of the British Empire, an honour
RT is an abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A cheese turned up wearing a medal, and someone checks that this is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft, white-rinded Normandy cheese is a named example of the general category.

clue.text: Make investment to join alliance

blocks.note: first meaning: lay siege to, which is what investing a town means
second, punning meaning: to be a leaguer, a member of a league

explanation.walkthrough: Investment here is the military sense, surrounding a fortress, not putting money in. The second half splits the word as 'be leaguer'.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest a town is to surround and besiege it with troops, cutting it off.

clue.text: Nominal place for press on board

blocks.note: first meaning: the top of a newspaper's front page, where its name is printed
second meaning: the top of a ship's mast

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nominal' means bearing a name, and 'the press' is newspapers; aboard ship the same word is the highest point of a mast.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper's title banner sits in this spot, and sailors use the term for the top of a ship's spar.

clue.text: Man's hereditary according to Hamlet

blocks.note: surface reading: something a man inherits, like a family trait
setter's reading: Hamlet lists the sorrows 'that flesh is heir to' in his soliloquy

explanation.surface: A question of what mankind inherits, settled by Shakespeare's prince.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'To be or not to be', Hamlet speaks of 'the heart-ache and the thousand natural shocks that flesh is heir to'; being heir to it makes it hereditary.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet names this emotional pain first among the afflictions that all human flesh inherits.

clue.text: Girl-sailors make divine visitors

blocks.note: Ava, a girl's name
tar is old slang for a sailor

explanation.surface: A girl and some sailors turn up as heavenly guests.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu belief these are incarnations of a god descending to earth, deities appearing in bodily form.

clue.text: Mistakes in the field hold back hounds

blocks.note: first meaning: small errors
second meaning: cricket fielders standing beside the wicketkeeper
third meaning: leashes that restrain dogs until released

explanation.surface: A huntsman's errors out in the countryside let the hounds go too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: Three meanings, not two. In cricket the slips are close fielders behind the batsman; a slip is also a dog's leash.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun covers small errors, a group of cricket fielding positions, and the leads used to restrain hunting dogs.

clue.text: No amateur international match? Objection!

blocks.note: someone who is not an amateur is a professional
a Test is an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.surface: Someone complains that an international game is being played by professionals.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name a formal statement of disapproval or dissent raised against something.

clue.text: Open campaign herein to set up temporary housing

indicators.note: herein says the answer lies inside the words right here in the clue

blocks.note: found inside the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: An army opens its campaign by pitching its tents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' tempts a reversal, but the letters run forwards; it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch tents and settle in a camp is to establish shelter that will not last long.

clue.text: Vote for Metropolitan Harbour Board, etc, revised

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so these letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the Port of London Authority, the capital's port body
taken as written

explanation.surface: Members cast a ballot on a revised proposal from London's port committee and similar bodies.
explanation.walkthrough: The PLA is the Port of London Authority, which runs the Thames docks.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'it pleases', this is the formal assent cast in a university or church assembly, a vote in favour.

clue.text: Where Warwickshire men, we hear, can still have cake

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the sense of a phrase is matched by its sound

blocks.note: if nothing has been consumed, you can still have your cake

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Warwickshire men are said to manage having their cake and eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: Nuneaton is a market town in Warwickshire, in the English Midlands; its name sounds like 'none eaten'.
explanation.definitionFit: This town lies in Warwickshire, so it is a place where people of that county live.

clue.text: Deceive lover with a torch

blocks.note: flam is an old verb meaning to trick or cheat
a beau is a boyfriend or admirer

explanation.surface: Someone cheats on a partner who still carries a torch for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover with a torch' suggests carrying a torch for someone; 'a torch' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing names a flaming torch, especially one with several wicks used in processions.

clue.text: Article with two points gives penetration

blocks.note: the indefinite article
cum is Latin for with, as in a kitchen-cum-diner
east and north, two compass points

explanation.surface: An item with two sharp tips is good for piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' and 'penetration' suggest something sharp; penetration here is mental sharpness.
explanation.definitionFit: Penetration in the sense of keen insight means the same as shrewdness and sharp judgement.

clue.text: " 1 " in numbers, for the numbers came" (Pope)

definitions.text: " 1 " in numbers, for the numbers came" (Pope)

blocks.note: surface reading: the digit one written among figures
setter's reading: Pope's Epistle to Arbuthnot, where numbers means verse he spoke as a child

explanation.surface: A line of Pope quoted with one word missing for the solver to supply.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's '1' is the start of Pope's line 'I lisp'd in numbers, for the numbers came', so the gap is the past tense of lisp.
explanation.definitionFit: Pope claims that as an infant he spoke in verse, uttering it in childish speech before he could talk properly.

clue.text: However doctored tapes are . distinct

indicators.note: doctored material has been tampered with, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Even edited recordings remain clearly identifiable.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are distinct stand apart from each other, not joined or mixed together.
